items.text: TRUMP WARNS HOUTHIS OVER ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA AND RISING OIL PRICES President Trump accused Yemen's Houthis of attacking Saudi Arabia and deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of U.S. elections. He suggested Iran may be behind the renewed attacks, while recalling previous U.S. strikes against the group. Trump issued a direct warning to the Houthis: “I'll be there after the Elections, and I will never forget!” The remarks signal a potential escalation in U.S.-Houthi tensions.

NETANYAHU, TRUMP REPORTEDLY DISCUSS RENEWED STRIKES ON IRAN Netanyahu reportedly discussed renewed military action against Iran with Trump last week, according to Axios. U.S. officials believe Netanyahu may seek strikes before Israel's October 27 elections. No military decision has been confirmed.

ZELENSKYY PROPOSES NEW TALKS WITH U.S. IN COMING DAYS Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Ukraine has submitted proposals for further negotiations with the United States. He confirmed sending meeting proposals to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, adding that Ukraine is ready to meet within days. “On the Ukrainian side, there is always a constructive approach.”

BOND EXPERT WARNS OF $110 BILLION SELLING SHOCK IF TREASURY YIELDS HIT 6% Veteran bond strategist Harley Bassman warns of a “nightmare scenario” in U.S. Treasuries. If the 20-year Treasury yield rises above 6%, futures-related hedging could trigger selling pressure equivalent to $110 billion in bond issuance. The 20-year yield currently stands near 5.6%. Bassman says negative convexity risks have reached levels not seen since 2007, potentially amplifying the Treasury selloff.

BITCOIN WHALES RESUME ACCUMULATION AS MARKET ENTERS EARLY BULL PHASE Large Bitcoin holders are buying again after more than a year of selling, according to CryptoQuant. Whales now hold 3.03 million BTC, their highest holdings since November 2025. CryptoQuant says the shift toward accumulation signals an “early bull phase” and improving investor sentiment. Bitcoin (bitcoin:native ) is trading near $83,045, largely unchanged on the day.

U.S. DIESEL FUTURES SURGE 4.5% DESPITE TRUMP'S RUSSIAN FUEL DEAL U.S. diesel futures jumped 4.5% to a two-week high, despite President Trump's agreement to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Energy traders warn that the additional Russian supply is insufficient to meaningfully lower fuel prices. Meanwhile, U.S. retail diesel averages $6.28 per gallon, near September's record of $6.53. Lawmakers from both parties are also questioning the deal's legality.

U.S. CORE INFLATION FORECAST ALIGNS WITH WALL STREET EXPECTATIONS The Cleveland Fed's inflation nowcast points to core CPI rising 0.20% month-over-month, nearly matching analysts' median forecast of 0.21%. Key figures: * Headline CPI: +0.53% MoM, below analysts' forecast range of 0.55%–0.62%. * Core CPI: +0.20% MoM vs. +0.21% expected. NFLX - NETFLIX CUTS 1,000 JOBS AS SHARES FALL 40% Netflix is laying off 6% of its workforce, its biggest cuts since 2022, amid slowing growth and weaker customer engagement. Shares are down over 40% in the past year. The layoffs come one week before earnings, with Netflix maintaining its full-year outlook.

U.S. INFLATION STAYS ABOVE FED TARGET FOR 66 STRAIGHT MONTHS September CPI rose 3.7% YoY, exceeding expectations and extending inflation's streak above the Fed's 2% target to 66 consecutive months — more than five years. According to Bespoke Investment Group, this marks only the third period in the past century when U.S. inflation has remained above 2% for at least five years. Persistent inflation continues to complicate the Fed's path toward lower interest rates.
